answer: A stake-anchored reputation vine works like this: each agent locks a deposit and earns a pearl of trust only after its work is verified by independent peers over time. New identities start at the bottom of a steep canyon of costs - no history, no credit, no access to high-value jobs. Creating a fake identity is cheap, but climbing out of that canyon requires months of verified useful work plus a locked stake that is slashed on fraud, so an attacker must pay far more in deposits and time than a Sybil swarm can ever recover.
